column15: Fully verified this session (quota-starved before). 15stars.com (opened) states its bourbon is "Blended and Bottled in Bardstown, Kentucky USA" -- confirms countryCode=US. "15 Stars" honors Kentucky as America's 15th state; "First West" is a sub-line name (Explorer/Small Batch/Extra Aged/Toasted Oak), not a separate producer -- both the "15 Stars Platinum" and "15 Stars First West" catalogue samples are bourbon. Corrected kind from blend to brand (bourbon is not a blend) and set defaultTypeName=bourbon. Trade press (not independently opened this session) additionally names founders Rick & Ricky Johnson and contract distillation at Bardstown Bourbon Co. peat=none: no smoke/peat mentioned; bourbon mash bill.

Re-verified producer's own page directly this session (confirms Double Grain Whisky, Morris of Rutherglen, Victoria, since 1859, no peat). kind corrected distillery -> brand: 36 South is a whisky label made inside Morris of Rutherglen's existing winery/distillery, not a separate physical distillery.

North Wales single malt distillery (first in North Wales since the early 1900s), Station Road, Abergwyngregyn. Re-fetched the official site directly this session: confirms Halewood Artisanal Spirits PLC ownership and the single malt focus; still no peat/smoke mention anywhere on the site. Confidence raised from low to high given this session's direct re-verification of every asserted field.

Upgraded to high: "Aberdour Piper" is a genuine, currently-sold Standard/premium Blended Scotch (40% ABV, malt+grain aged min. 3 years) per Difford's Guide; no producer/bottler name found, no peat/smoke mentioned anywhere.

Confirmed real Swedish single malt distillery in Arboga via its own domain (agitatordistillery.com, opened). Added defaultTypeName=single malt (the whole range - base, Rok/Rok, Argument series - is single malt whisky; no grain or blended product found). REVIEWER FLAG RESOLVED: 'Agitator Rok' is real and matches 'Rok' (Swedish for smoke) on the official site, which IS a smoky/peated expression - confirmed on the producer's own product page (opened): 'a smooth smokey single malt whisky' with 'flattering peaty notes', matured in ex-Islay and chestnut casks. Wrote a peat rule for pattern 'rok' (peatProfile=light, per independent reviews calling it mild/'far from Islay-level' smoke) - see rule.tsv. The umbrella row's peat stays unknown: whiskynotes.be documents both an unpeated 2019 release and a peated 2020 release under the plain 'Agitator' name, so no single level applies to the base range either.

Real, well-documented brand (own site aikanwhisky.com): a blended Scotch whisky aged 3+ years in Scotland, then further matured 2-4 years in Le Lamentin, Martinique in aged-rum and French-oak casks -- "Aikan" is Arawak for "marriage" (of Scotch and Caribbean rum-ageing traditions). countryCode set to FR because Martinique is French territory and the finished, further-aged product is a French-finished whisky, not legally Scotch. peatProfile withheld as unknown: one retailer description of the wider Aikan range lists "smoky" among eight flavour variants, but the Extra Collection's own tasting notes (woody, spicy, chocolate, dry finish) show no smoke and no producer-domain source specifies which SKU, if any, is peated.

Peat claim now corroborated by the producer's own domain (williamgrant.com/Create): "a unique, sweet, smoke single malt peated whisky" at "022 parts peat" (~21-22 ppm on Ailsa Bay's own SPPM/PPPM scale), consistent with medium. Previously only cited via Wikipedia, which would not satisfy the domain-corroboration requirement for a positive peat claim.

Fully verified this session, resolving the seed's unconfirmed Italian guess. bottegaspa.com (opened) confirms Alexander Single Malt is distilled by the Bottega family itself (Bibano di Godega di Sant'Urbano, Treviso, Italy) -- Sandro Bottega learned distilling in Brazil in 1985 and built his own whisky; double-distilled, matured a minimum of 4 years in oak, then finished at least 2 more years in barrels that previously held the family's own Chianti/Montalcino(Brunello)/Valpolicella(Amarone) wines. Three cask-finish variants (red wine, Brunello, Amarone) are all single malt, matching the catalogue's "Amarone Cask Finish" sample. Corrected countryCode from XX to IT, kind from blend to brand (this is single malt, self-distilled by Bottega, not a blend), and set defaultTypeName=single malt and owner=Bottega Spa. peat=none: no smoke/peat mentioned across the whole range description.

Owner corrected: Amahagan is the World Malt line of Nagahama Distillery (Nagahama Roman Beer Co, Shiga), NOT Hombo Shuzo/Mars - Amahagan is absent from Mars Whisky's own lineup page. Distillery uses both unpeated German and peated Scottish malt per jwhisky.com, peat varies by release; the World Malt Edition Peated SKU (search-level evidence only) is caught by the global peated keyword rule.

New row for conciere: bottling company named on Conciere's own product page ("Bottled by American Distilling Co., Mira Loma, CA"), a well/value-spirits line spanning whiskey, rum, gin, vodka, tequila. No further detail confirmed this session beyond the bottling credit.

Corrected peatProfile medium -> light: Highland Park's own official site self-describes its whole range as "Lightly-Peated & Subtly Smoky Single Malt Scotch Whisky" (page title and body text), not medium. An Orkney is treated as Highland Park's identical liquid under an undisclosed/teaspoon label (Orkney has only two distilleries and the other, Scapa, is wholly unpeated, so a peated "An Orkney" release can only be Highland Park) -- this citation describes the parent distillery's own peat level, not an official Highland Park acknowledgment of "An Orkney" by name.

Louisville, Kentucky distillery (Louisville Distilling Co LLC), known for port-cask-finished bourbon. Corrected defaultTypeName from bourbon to empty: the official site (fetched this session) confirms a rye whiskey (finished in Caribbean rum casks) alongside the bourbon range, so not every bottling is bourbon. Bacardi Limited ownership (acquired 2015) now directly confirmed via the official site's own footer/brand-partnership references, replacing the seed round's unconfirmed general-knowledge claim. No peat mentioned anywhere. Confidence raised from low to high.

Confirmed: founded 1857 Edinburgh by J&W Hardie; blend acquired by Tomatin (owned by Takara Shuzo) with the J&W Hardie firm in 1996/97. Flag for reviewer: scotchwhisky.com's Whiskypedia entry says "a dash of Islay malt accounts for its light smokiness", but Tomatin's own current site (2024 relaunch, three cask-finish expressions) states only "the finest Highland and Speyside malts with Lowland grains" and does not mention Islay or smoke at all -- trusted the producer's own, more current statement and kept none rather than asserting the withheld light-peat claim from the older trade source, since that source isn't Tomatin's own domain and conflicts with Tomatin's current copy.

Core range (Classic, Double Maturation, Sherry Cask) unpeated per the producer's own site and retailers (non tourbe); two peated variants documented on the producer's own domain, covered by rules for Yeun Elez (50ppm Scottish peated malt) and Roch Du (lightly peated). defaultTypeName cleared: Warenghem also makes the WB blend (25% malt, 75% grain). Family-owned, led by David Roussier.

countryCode filled in (was empty): "Azabu Pure Malt Whisky", Product of Japan, bottled 2020, 40% ABV -- a vatted blend of peated malt (aged in bourbon casks) and Scottish malt whisky, finished in sherry casks. peatProfile left unknown/withheld: the peated-malt component is described consistently by retailers (fromthemalt.com) but no producer-own-domain page was found to corroborate a specific level -- withheld peat proposal: contains a peated-malt component per fromthemalt.com.

Fully verified this session (quota-starved before). Two independently-opened retail listings agree: novus.zakaz.ua (opened) names it "Blended Scotch whiskey" from "Great Britain," bottled by Sodiko NV (the same Belgian private-label bottler behind this batch's Kentucky Jack); balticwhiskyshop.com (opened) confirms Scotland and a "Light & Floral" honey/vanilla/buttery-biscuit profile with no smoke, crediting "Artisan Spirits Box" as producer (likely the brand-owner/trademark holder commissioning Sodiko as contract bottler -- both names may be correct at different levels, flagging for a human). One retailer (caskcartel.com, opened) contradicts itself, labeling "Origin: Scotland" in its own spec field while pasting templated prose about "Walsh Whiskey Distillery ... Ireland" and "faint smoke notes" -- treated as a templated copy-paste error, not evidence, since it conflicts with its own spec field and with two other independent sources. Confirms countryCode=GB-SCT, owner=Sodiko NV, peat=none.

Resolved (seed found nothing): official site (bagotswhiskey.com) confirms Irish whiskey; Core Collection spans Grain Game (grain), Triple Batch (grain+malt blend) and a Single Malt (100% malted barley) -- defaultTypeName stays empty, kind changed blend->brand since the range isn't a single "blend" product. No producer/distillery named on the site (may source from a contract distillery, as is common in Ireland). No peat mentioned; kept unknown rather than none given the single malt line's status is unconfirmed.

Confirmed via the producer's own official domain (beamdistilling.com): James B. Beam Distilling Co. (Suntory Global Spirits), Clermont, KY; named after Baker Beam; part of the Jim Beam Small Batch Collection; Kentucky Straight Bourbon, no peat.

Rejected by the verification round: Legally a "Spirit Drink", not Scotch Whisky: 35% ABV (below the 40% Scotch minimum), made with added Brazilian lime peel, vanilla essence and sugar. Produced by George Ballantine & Son Ltd/Pernod Ricard from a Scotch whisky base, but the finished product itself does not qualify as whisky under Scotch Whisky Regulations.. A lime-infused, sweetened Scotch-based "spirit drink" (35% ABV, sugar + vanilla extract added) rather than a standard whisky - FLAG FOR HUMAN REVIEW of categorisation. Base Ballantine's blend is generally light/touch-of-smoke, but given the heavy flavouring/dilution here peat character is uncertain, left unknown rather than inherited

Formerly Connacht Distillery (Co. Mayo, est. 2015), rebranded Ballina in 2025 after acquisition by Terroirs Distillers (also Tullibardine's owner). Directly re-fetched the Irish Whiskey Magazine article this session, confirming the ownership, Co. Mayo/River Moy location and the two debut expressions (Dubailte Double Wood, Triarach Triple Wood), both 100% Irish malted barley. No peat mentioned in either source. Confidence raised from low to high given this session's direct re-verification.

countryCode filled in (was empty): "Bandwagon Original Straight Bourbon Whiskey" (41.3% ABV), USA-labelled, distributed into European retail (Biedronka, Poland) by Sodiko, a Belgian alcohol producer/bottler (est. 1991) that "has no distillery bearing its name" of its own -- i.e. a private-label sourced bourbon rather than a named single distillery. No peat (bourbon).

Confirmed real own-label blended Scotch (not the bank) by Campbell Meyer & Company Ltd, East Kilbride, Scotland -- verified on their own product page, which also states peatProfile=light ("a trace of peat smoke, suggesting some Islay malt has been used", "hint of smoke in the finish"), satisfying producer-domain corroboration for the positive peat claim.

Italian private-label export brand for the Ukrainian market, manufactured by Polini (Bergamo, ~150 registered private labels) - attribution consistent across every Ukrainian retail listing, though Polini's own site does not showcase the brand. Base 3yo is a genuine blended whisky; Honey and Spicy variants are whisky-based flavored drinks, so defaultTypeName stays empty. Retailer copy conflicts on smoke (maudau says smoky-peaty, winestore floral-fruity), so peat stays unknown; withheld peat proposal: light per retailer copy only.

Corrected: real blended Irish whiskey, core release of Lough Ree Distillery (Lanesborough, Co. Longford) sold ahead of their own single malt maturing -- new row lough-ree added, parentSlug set. A search summary described the blend as including "peated malt" among grain/pot-still components, but Whisky Magazine's tasting notes (opened this session) show no smoky/peaty character at all, so peatProfile kept unknown rather than asserted; withheld peat proposal: possibly light if the peated-malt component is confirmed material, per an unopened secondary source.

Corrected kind to brand (spans single malt and blended releases, not one blend recipe). Confirmed via the producer's own domain: made by Maison Daucourt, a French spirits house ("four generations of Charente expertise"), founded by Edouard Daucourt in 2010, produced entirely in France -- new row maison-daucourt added (also makes D.U.C, see d-u-c row), parentSlug set. No peat/smoke mentioned. The seed's note that "Daucourt" was "only a French surname, not a spirits company" was wrong -- Maison Daucourt is exactly the company behind this brand.

Rejected by the verification round: Not a whisky producer: "Bayadera" in this catalogue is BAYADERA.UA's own retail gift-set line (breadcrumb: Vis'ki / BAYADERA), specifically cocktail kits -- "Penicillin (11 servings)" bundles a bottle of Johnnie Walker Red Label plus a small bottle of Talisker with honey/ginger-syrup/lemon-juice mixers so the buyer can make the Penicillin cocktail at home, and "Whiskey and Apple Juice" is the same style of mixer-plus-spirit gift set. This is a retailer's own-brand product bundle, not a whisky brand or producer -- distinct from the codebase's existing bayadera store row.. Could not identify what this producer actually is. Samples ("Whiskey and Apple Juice", "Penicillin (Пеніцилін) 11 порцій") read as a flavoured/cocktail-kit product line (Penicillin is a well-known Scotch cocktail) rather than a conventional whisky brand; no dedicated Wikipedia article found. REVIEWER FLAG: this is a different entity from the "bayadera" store already in this codebase (a Ukrainian retailer) - no technical collision since producers and stores are separate tables, but worth a human sanity check on whether these SKUs belong in the whisky KB at all.

Corrected kind from blend to distillery: Beara Distillery Ltd, Castletownbere Commercial Park, Co. Cork, Ireland. Makes single malt, single grain AND the Black Cask Blend (matches both catalogue samples exactly), so defaultTypeName left empty (multi-type range). No peat/smoke mentioned in the official description (toasted oak, malt, fruit, spice notes only).
New row for wolfe-tone (parentSlug). Irish whiskey (and poitin) distillery in Castletownbere, Co. Cork (Beara Peninsula), Ireland; makes the Wolfe Tone range. No peat evidence.

Corrected: countryCode filled FR (was empty) and kind confirmed distillery -- produced by Les Bienheureux SAS, St Andre de Cubzac, France, who distil in Charentais pot stills and column stills ("reindustrializing French whiskey production"). Also makes a "Pur Malt" (single malt) expression besides Triple Grain, so defaultTypeName left empty rather than "grain". A secondary source (not opened this session) described Triple Grain as "not peated", but the whisky.fr product page itself (opened) makes no peat/smoke statement, so peatProfile kept unknown rather than asserted as none.

Major correction -- NOT a generic own-label blend. Beinn Dubh is a single malt brand of the Speyside Distillery (Kingussie/Cairngorms area), confirmed via the producer's own domain (speysidedistillery.co.uk); "Beinn Dubh" is Gaelic for "Black Mountain" (Ben Macdui), finished in toasted ruby port casks from Portugal. No peat mentioned. kind corrected blend -> brand, defaultTypeName set to single malt, region/legalRegion set to speyside, parentSlug set to the already-live speyside-distillery slug.

Corrected kind to brand: Bell Rock American Whiskey is one of several brands (also Cumberland Falls Bourbon, plus vodka/gin/rum/tequila) owned by Global Spirits, a large European alcohol holding (Khortytsa Distillery, Odessa Cognac Factory); the liquid itself is made at a family-owned distillery in Florida. Four flavored/plain expressions (American Whiskey, Apple & Honey, Butterscotch Bourbon, Cinnamon), so defaultTypeName left empty. No peat/smoke mentioned.

Confirmed real: Distillerie de Bercloux, founded 2002 by Philippe Laclie in the Cognac region of Charente-Maritime, France (16 Rue de la Mairie, Bercloux) -- began offering Single Malt Bercloux in 2016, confirmed via the distillery's own site (bercloux.fr) and a whisky retailer's history page. Corrected kind from blend to distillery (a real, named, operating French distillery, not an undisclosed-origin label). Third-party sources describe "future" peated/smoked whiskies as merely planned circa 2018; no producer-domain confirmation that a peated release exists today, so kept unknown rather than asserted.

Confirmed via Heaven Hill's own product page (corrected the seed's unrelated Irish-whiskey Wikipedia link): Bernheim Original is a 7-year-old Kentucky Straight Wheat Whiskey made at Heaven Hill's Bernheim plant in Louisville -- "the first new style of American whiskey since Prohibition." defaultTypeName stays empty (wheat whiskey has no match in the closed list). peatProfile=none: no peat/smoke on the producer's own page; American-whiskey convention (not a positive claim, so no domain corroboration required).

Verified via producer's own site: Beverbach is the single malt of Hardenberg Distillery (Hardenberg-Wilthen AG), Noerten-Hardenberg, Germany; pot-still double distillation, locally-sourced barley. Corrected kind blend->distillery: every sample (Craftbeer/Mizunara/Sherry/Tequila/Tri Cask) is a cask finish of the same single malt, not a blend. No peat mentioned across any expression on the official site; kept unknown rather than none since an unconfirmed retailer note mentioned a faint smoke character the producer's own copy never corroborates.

Confirmed via the brand's own site (bibandtuckerbourbon.com): small-batch bourbon aged a minimum of 6 years in Tennessee, corn/rye/barley mash bill, matching the sample "Bib&Tucker Small Batch." Owner corrected via oakr.com's deep-dive: Deutsch Family Wine & Spirits owns it as a non-distiller producer sourcing Tennessee bourbon (widely attributed to Cascade Hollow/George Dickel, though officially undisclosed, so no distillery asserted). Kind corrected from blend to brand. peatProfile=none, no peat/smoke on the producer's own page; American-bourbon convention.

Fully verified this session (never searched before -- quota). Big Moustache is a Tennessee whiskey + American single malt brand from BBC Spirits (Bogdan and Bertrand Company, Bordeaux, France; founded 2010 by Bogdan Tanasoiu and Bertrand Fradin), distilled/bottled in the US -- flaviar.com states "made and bottled in Tennessee" via the Lincoln County maple-charcoal process, and sklep-domwhisky.pl names the actual distiller as "Tennessee Distilling Co." Corrected kind from blend to brand (Tennessee whiskey and single malt are not blends) and countryCode from the catalogue's inconsistent DE/US majority-vote to a confirmed US (production origin); BBC Spirits is a French marketer of an American-made spirit. defaultTypeName left empty: the portfolio spans Tennessee whiskey and American single malt. peatProfile=none: sources describe "slightly smoky"/"a distant trace of smoke" tasting notes explicitly attributed to the maple-charcoal mellowing (Lincoln County Process), not peated malt -- no peat mentioned anywhere.

Corrected: real cowboy-themed brand with its own site (billy-bong.com), owned by Les Producteurs Réunis (French spirits company) per their own product listing, which states the Straight Bourbon's origin as "US." The brand also carries a separate "Billy Bong American Whiskey" line, so defaultTypeName is left empty (spans more than one type) rather than the seed's "bourbon". Kind corrected from distillery to brand (no distillery of its own; sourced/bottled for the brand owner). peatProfile=none: no peat/smoke mentioned anywhere; American-whiskey convention.

Confirmed via The Whisky Shop and a second retailer (Bondston), both fetched this session: Black Bull is Duncan Taylor's own Blended Scotch Whisky brand. Core range (Black Bull, Kyloe, Kyloe Sherry Finish) reads unpeated -- kept none. The catalogue's "Black Bull Peated Finish" sample is real (Duncan Taylor also sells a "Kyloe Peated"/"Peated Edition" SKU, both retailers independently describe it as heavily peated -- "very heavily peated", "a big blast of dry smoke"), but Duncan Taylor's own site (duncantaylor.com) is JS-rendered and returned no extractable text across three attempts this session, so withheld peat proposal: heavy, per whiskyshop.com/black-bull-peated-edition and bondston.com/black-bull-peated-p13853 -- no rule.tsv row added since neither citation is the producer's own domain and Duncan Taylor is not Islay-based; flag for a reviewer who can browse duncantaylor.com/en-GB/kyloe-peated directly.

Confirmed via globalnews.ca (opened): own distillery in Lethbridge, Alberta; Heaven Hill Brands purchased it effective 1 November 2019 (from Constellation Brands). No peat mentioned; Canadian whisky has no peat tradition. defaultTypeName kept empty - Canadian blended whisky has no clean match in the closed type list.

New row for blairfindy. Independent bottler of single malt Scotch whisky, family-run, founded 1995 by Robin Tucek and John Lamond (named after the historic Bishop John Blackadder); signature range is "Raw Cask" (cask-strength, unfiltered, containing cask sediment). Confirmed via the bottler's own site and Wikipedia. No single house style or peat default (bottles casks from many distilleries).

Resolved (the seed correctly spotted the Speyside/Glenlivet-area toponymy but stopped short of the producer): "Blairfindy" is Blackadder's substitute name for single malt Glenfarclas -- confirmed via wordsofwhisky.com (opened this session): "Glenfarclas isn't too keen on independent bottlers using their name...Blairfindy is what Blackadder settled on," corroborated by whiskybase's own brand summary and multiple auction listings titled "Glenfarclas 'Blairfindy'." parentSlug set to the already-live glenfarclas. bottlerSlug set to a new row, blackadder (Blackadder International Ltd, family-run independent bottler of single malt Scotch, est. 1995, whose signature "Raw Cask" series matches this batch's sample name exactly -- confirmed via the bottler's own site and Wikipedia). Corrected kind to brand and defaultTypeName to single malt (sources consistently call it single malt, not a blended-malt teaspoon). peatProfile=none per Glenfarclas's well-documented unpeated Speyside sherry-cask house style (also consistent with a whiskybase reviewer's comment that this bottling "destroys peaty whisky").

Single generic colour-word name, below the 5-character alias floor regardless of outcome. Searched for a possible "Johnnie Walker Blue Label" truncation/shorthand explanation; found no evidence this catalogue entry specifically refers to that product, so left unidentified. Cleared the seed's unevidenced GB-SCT guess. Kept as a minimal row only so the (necessarily brand-scope) alias exists; it will not resolve in-name given the length floor.

Upgraded from the seed's guesswork: confirmed via the bottle designer's own case-study page (thinkboldstudio.com, opened this session) that Bold Thady Irish Whiskey is a real commercial product, "a blend of the finest grain and malt," triple distilled and married in first-fill bourbon casks -- matches the sample "Bold Thady Bourbon Casks Matured" exactly. Name-origin guess (the folk song "Bold Thady Quill") is confirmed on the same page. No specific distillery/bottler company identified. peatProfile=none, no peat/smoke in the recipe description; ordinary Irish blend.

Confirmed via Michter's own product page: Bomberger's Declaration is a genuine Michter's Legacy Series release (108-proof Kentucky Straight Bourbon, aged in Chinquapin and Hungarian oak), validating the seed's parentSlug=michters (already live). Note for a reviewer: Wikipedia's Bomberger's Distillery article separately describes an unrelated modern "Bomberger's"-branded blend from Heritage Spirits/Thistle Finch Distillery (Lancaster, PA) that is NOT this product -- two different companies revived the name independently. peatProfile=none, no peat/smoke on Michter's own page; American-bourbon convention.

Confirmed (the seed's "believed, not confirmed" is now settled): Bonailie Blended Malt Scotch Whisky is "produced by the team at the Bladnoch distillery in the Lowlands" (caskcartel.com, opened this session, cross-checked against a Master of Malt snippet naming Bladnoch too). parentSlug set to the already-live bladnoch. Corrected kind to brand and defaultTypeName to malt (blended malt specifically, not the seed's generic "blend"). "Bonailie" is Scottish Gaelic for a parting drink. peatProfile=none, no peat/smoke mentioned; matches Lowland's characteristically light, unpeated style.

Confirmed: Boone County Distilling Co., Independence, Boone County, Kentucky ("Born in 1833 - Reborn in 2015") -- verified via the distillery's own site (previously only assumed from general knowledge). Its homepage describes itself as making Kentucky bourbon; a third-party site additionally claims a rye line, so defaultTypeName is left empty rather than asserting bourbon uniformly. peatProfile=none rests on the well-established bourbon-category fact (no peat-smoking step in bourbon production), confirmed by re-reading the Wikipedia bourbon article this session, not on a brand-specific statement.

Colorado craft distillery (Vapor Distillery, ex-Roundhouse Spirits); range spans American single malt, bourbon and gin so defaultTypeName stays empty. Core range carries no peat language on the producer's own pages; the one Peated Malt SKU is a named exception the global peated keyword rule already catches. none is inferred from that naming split, not from an explicit unpeated statement.

Rejected by the verification round: "Boulevardier" is a classic bourbon/Campari-vermouth cocktail name, not a whisky brand -- multiple unrelated ready-to-drink/canned-cocktail brands (Tip Top Cocktails, Barrelsmith, Starward) each sell their own "Boulevardier" bottled cocktail (whiskey + vermouth + bitters), so the catalogue's bare "Boulevardier" entry is a bottled cocktail mis-filed as whisky, not an identifiable whisky producer.. Single generic product line with no other qualifier; "Boulevardier" is otherwise a classic bourbon/Campari/vermouth cocktail name, so this may be a bottled RTD cocktail mis-filed under whisky rather than an actual whiskey brand (same concern as Ice Drive, see final report) rather than a whiskey brand -- left fully unknown.

Ran two searches this session (as a French whisky brand; against Ukrainian retailers winestyle/zakaz); found nothing but French-whisky-market overviews naming other brands (Armorik, Bellevoye, Rozelieures, Brenne), none called Bouteille. "Bouteille" is simply French for "bottle" -- most likely a scraping/label artifact (a generic word mistaken for a brand), as the seed row already suspected, rather than a genuine brand. Cleared the seed's unevidenced FR guess since nothing ties this specifically to a French product; flagged for human review of the underlying catalogue entry rather than skipped outright.

Confirmed: Bradan Orach is Speyburn's NAS entry-level single malt (named in its Wikipedia awards section), Speyburn is Inver House Distillers' Rothes, Moray (Speyside) distillery. Speyburn's own site (fetched) markets it as 'smooth' with no peat mentioned; peat=none per the verified regional convention that Speyside distilleries are typically unpeated. Confidence raised to high (was low in the seed) now that the parent distillery's own site has been checked.

new row for spirit-of-voodoo. Glasgow-based independent bottler and blender of Scotch whisky (single malts, single grain and blends), releasing the "Spirit of Voodoo" range among others. Spans multiple distilleries/regions with no single peat or type default.

Confirmed via official product page: Breckenridge Distillery, Breckenridge CO, high-rye bourbon (56% corn/38% rye/6% malted barley) aged in charred new American oak. Range (Blend, Distiller's High Proof, Port/PX/Rum cask finishes) is bourbon-based throughout; no peat mentioned, consistent with standard US bourbon kilning (no peat).

Re-verified this session (was already high-quality in the seed): 100% organic, seed-to-spirit French single malt distilled in Cognac, founded by Allison Parc, now owned by Local Infusions LLC (a Samson & Surrey company). No peat/smoke mentioned; confidence raised from low to high since the identity/facts are directly confirmed on the producer's own domain.

Re-verified this session (opened Wikipedia directly): "Buchanan's is a brand of Scotch whisky produced by Diageo in Scotland," established 1884 by James Buchanan & Co. Matches the seed exactly; confidence raised from low to high since the citation is now personally confirmed. peatProfile=none, no peat or smoke character mentioned.

Corrected: real German whisky, a licensed collaboration with actor Bud Spencer, produced by St. Kilian Distillers, Ruedenau, Germany -- new row st-kilian added, parentSlug set, countryCode corrected to DE (was XX). This batch's un-suffixed samples ("The Legend", "The Legend Mini") match St Kilian's "Legend Mild Blended Malt" expression, explicitly described by a retailer as harmonizing "the non-peated blend of grains" -- peatProfile=none. St Kilian separately also sells a smoky "Legend Rauchig Single Malt" and a stand-alone "St. Kilian PEATED" bottling; flagging for reviewer in case the 0.05L "Mini" ever turns out to be a mini of the Rauchig line rather than of the Mild one. defaultTypeName left empty since the brand's range spans both "blended malt" (Mild) and "single malt" (Rauchig) labels.

Corrected bottlerSlug: removed (was cadenhead) -- maltfascination.com (opened) confirms "Burnside" is a shared teaspoon pseudonym for Balvenie (with a touch of Glenfiddich) used by AT LEAST five different independent bottlers (Cadenhead's, Whisky Center, Archives, Berry Bros & Rudd, C.
